messages:
Priya Nair: FYI — we're seeing a >2x monthly bill jump for trace egress after the last rollout. Most of the volume is from fanout to Tempo + Splunk.
Alex Chen: Oof. Any quick numbers? rough breakdown?
Priya Nair: Rough: 65% to Tempo (retained 7d), 30% to Splunk (30d), rest to Honeycomb. Splunk ingestion is the cost driver for a few big customers.
Sam Renshaw: Are we currently doing fanout at the agent side or at the collector? That changes the options.
Vincent Lo: Right now the collector does the fanout: we export one canonical span blob and collector copies to configured backends.
Maya Kapoor: That means we pay network + backend cost for every copy even if downstream will drop it. We should consider routing earlier.
Alex Chen: Debate: sample/rate-limit at the SDK/agent versus at collector. SDK/agent sampling reduces egress but loses the ability to route different samples to different vendors per-org.
Sam Renshaw: Also agent sampling breaks consistency for linked spans (traces across services) unless we coordinate sampling keys.
Priya Nair: Proposal A: keep collector fanout but add per-org retention override + cheap-signature-based selective fanout. Only high-signal spans (error, latency>S) get copied to expensive backends.
Vincent Lo: Proposal B: move routing decisions to the agent with a small routing table: per-org backend list + per-route sample rates. Pros: saves egress, cons: more config surface and rollout complexity.
Alex Chen: For rollout UX we need console controls: a retention slider, a per-backend toggle, and a preview cost estimate (tokens/ingest units).
Maya Kapoor: +1 on preview cost. Product can show a monthly delta when you change retention or add Splunk as a backend.
Sam Renshaw: Technical note: selective fanout needs an efficient predicate. Suggest using simple attrs: span.kind, status.code, attributes.{http.status_code}, and a small regex on service.name.
Priya Nair: Example routing config prototype:
```
routing:
  - match: org:acme
    backend: splunk
    retention_days: 30
    condition: "(status.code >= 500) || (http.status_code >= 500)"
  - match: default
    backend: tempo
    retention_days: 7
```
Vincent Lo: If we deploy that naive config at collector, we're still duplicating full payloads to Splunk for matching spans. Would prefer predicate applied before making the copy.
Alex Chen: Could we do a cheap pre-filtering pass in the collector that only materializes copy when condition true? I think yes — parse minimal attributes, evaluate predicate, then copy.
Maya Kapoor: UI question: do we expose condition expressions directly (advanced mode) or provide canned rules (errors, p50/p95, specific services)?
Priya Nair: Recommend canned rules + advanced expression editor for power users. Keep defaults safe.
Sam Renshaw: We also need retention metadata per span export so backends know TTL. Tempo uses retention at the storage level; Splunk gets a separate ingestion pipeline.
Alex Chen: About sampling: we discussed per-org sampled traces for analytics vs full traces for debugging. Idea: retain full traces for a short window for all orgs (7d) and allow extended retention as a paid feature.
Vincent Lo: Ops concern: we must avoid high-cardinality attribute evaluation in the hot path. Precomputing tag keys for predicates would help.
Priya Nair: Edge case: cross-org traces (shared infra/span parents). We need a consistent decision to avoid partial traces. Suggest: trace-level determinations based on a single authoritative org tag (e.g., resource.attributes.organization_id).
Sam Renshaw: If org tag missing, fallback to collector default routing and mark trace as "split-risk" for debugging.
Maya Kapoor: For the console rollout flow: create a modal that previews downstream impacts, warns about potential partial-trace risk, and suggests canarying the policy.
deploy-bot: collector/exporter/tempo - health OK; splunk-exporter - 502 errors in last 5m :rotating_light:
Alex Chen: Thanks @deploy-bot — that's probably the immediate cost spike source. We should throttle retries and queue depth to avoid amplification.
Priya Nair: Action items: 1) RFC for selective-fanout at collector with predicate evaluation (Sam + Vincent). 2) Console mockups for retention slider + cost preview (Maya). 3) Short-term: add a Splunk throttle and backoff (Alex).
Sam Renshaw: I'll open the RFC draft today, include perf budget numbers and predicate evaluation benchmarks.
Vincent Lo: I'll prototype a pre-filter pass that reads only resource/span attrs required by predicates.
Maya Kapoor: Will mock console screens and a canary flow; will include copy for "partial trace" warnings.
Alex Chen: Can we aim to ship the backoff change as a hotfix this week? I'll take it.
Priya Nair: Great. Let's reconvene once RFC + mockups exist. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
__notes: thread generated: telemetry routing, retention, vendor integrations, fanout vs agent sampling debate.
